lore.13: Refounded the Mage Guild in the early 1900s with the backing of Britannia's royal house, styling it as a pseudo-chivalric order, hence the Sir and Lady titles its leaders still carry. As of 2001 he stands as one of the Guild's three pillars, representing the past, and has simply refused to ever step down; no one in the Guild can truly stand against him, since he knows spells even the gods do not.
lore.11: Born Joseph Ratzinger, he ascended to the Throne of Peter as Pietro II after John Paul II died from the assassination attempt of May 13, 1981. He has declared war on Jenna of Northpoint, refusing to recognize her as the Second Coming and branding her the Antichrist instead.
lore.10: His name is printed on tens of billions of banknotes and financial transaction logs, more times than the name of God across every printed Bible. The euro's security strip is laced with flecks of Fantablack scraped from the Omega Tower's outer walls, and between that arcane residue and the law that names are power, Draghi ascended as the godhead of the market itself, an abstract concept now driving the multiverse's economy from behind the scenes.
lore.6: Current president of the Free States of Midwest, one of the three fragments the Americas were split into after independence never fully happened: the Republic of Cascadia on the east coast, the Free States of Midwest in the center, and the Atlantic Protectorate on the west coast under Britannia's control.
lore.5: Head of the European Space Agency, currently testing new rockets built almost entirely from armor plating meant to be chewed apart by orbital debris, buying astronauts just enough time to clear low orbit. The Kessler Syndrome triggered during the Y2K event turned any ordinary launch into a coin flip with over 90% odds of failure.
lore.1: A mechanic from Westford, Texas, and something of a living legend. Built the Liminal Engine himself, a device that chews through dimensional energy and lets him drive across realities in a battered camper he calls The Beast. He once spent years running Route 666 with Eris, the goddess of discord, robbing banks by having her bend probability to crack any safe.
lore.9001: Learned the craft from someone who is no longer around to be asked about it. Half the spells work, and so far the half that do not have been the more interesting ones.
lore.9002: Sells out rooms by losing badly on purpose, then wins the one nobody put money on. The knee is held together with tape and conviction.
lore.9003: Loads a spell into every chamber and has never once explained where the bullets go. The warrens turn out plenty of theorists; this one shoots.
lore.9004: A puddle with opinions. Whatever it was before it started imitating other things, it is honestly a little vague on the details itself.
lore.9005: Swore the oath in front of witnesses, which is the part that makes it binding. The armour was already secondhand when it was handed over.
lore.9006: Hears the sentence a moment before it is said, and has learned not to answer early. It is exhausting at parties.
lore.9007: Plays rooms that hold nine people and talks about them as though they held nine hundred. One of those numbers will be true eventually.
lore.9008: Works a small enchantment into everything that leaves the workshop, most of them harmless. The kettle has opinions now.
lore.9009: Calls things, and they come, which is only half the difficulty. Getting them to leave again is the part the books skip.
lore.9010: Left the order on good terms, or so the letter says, and still keeps the hours. The faith survived the paperwork better than the paperwork survived her.

0: The branch behind her is a world where magic was never filed away among fairy tales but licensed, taxed and printed in the back pages of the newspapers.
Her dimension burned its last cathedral in 1913 and has run on borrowed miracles ever since.
The world she left was one flooded city ninety storeys tall, with the sea held back by recited law.
She grew up in a country that had quietly seceded from geography and could only be reached by getting lost on purpose.
In her reality the Y2K event never stopped, and it has been the first of January for eighteen months.
Her home branch is a Europe stitched together out of company towns, each one owned by a different sleeping god.
She arrives from a world where nobody died between 1971 and 1994, and everyone is still deciding whether that was a mercy.
The dimension behind her ran the Solomonic Ritual twelve times, industrially, and made a national holiday out of it.
Her reality never invented the wheel and never needed to, since distance there is a matter of persuasion.
She is from a timeline where the moon is a settled place and the night sky is crowded with lamps that answer to names.
1: There she was a licensed weather-witch, salting clouds for farming consortia.
She spent that life as a night nurse in a hospice for people whose deaths had gone missing.
She was the youngest archivist ever admitted to that world's Mage Guild, and the only one expelled from it twice.
In that life she was a courier, carrying sealed words between cities that refused to speak to each other.
She was a hedge-witch working out of a laundrette, doing curses at the going rate and never asking names.
There she was crowned, briefly, by a country that regretted it within the season.
She was that world's last practising exorcist, mostly employed by landlords.
She made her living reading the market by candlelight for men who called it research.
In that branch she taught primary-school arithmetic, and quietly held the town's bridge together with it.
She was a soldier there, in a war fought entirely by correspondence.
2: Then something in the sky opened a door that opened the wrong way, and she was on the far side of it.
It ended when she signed a contract she had not finished reading, and the ink outlived the world.
The end came as a sound, one long note, and everything that could hear it stopped being there.
She stepped into a lift going down and stepped out somewhere with a different number of directions.
A god she had never petitioned answered anyway, and the answer took the whole street with it.
She traded her dimension away in a wager she still insists she won.
The Liminal Engine of that world was switched on for testing, once, and she was standing too close.
Her name was written into someone else's ritual, and names are power, so she went where the name went.
Something enormous began remembering her, and the pressure of being remembered pushed her out.
She followed a stranger with her own face through a gap in a hedge, and the hedge closed.
3: She kept everything except the reason for any of it.
Ninety-two percent of her memories went into the payment; she does not know which ones, only that she flinches at church bells.
She lost her mother tongue in transit and has been borrowing this one ever since.
What she paid was her death, which now belongs to somebody else and is being kept badly.
She left with the clothes she stood in, a spear she cannot lift, and no proof she ever existed.
The crossing took her age; she is thirty-something and eleven at once, depending on the hour.
She surrendered every face she loved, and kept, uselessly, all of their birthdays.
Her shadow stayed behind, so she has learned to stand where nobody checks.
She gave up the last forty years of her own future and has not decided whether to miss them.
The toll was her talent, which grew back wrong, and much larger.
4: She turned up here on a road she does not remember choosing, and calls that a beginning.
Now she is on this branch, cataloguing the differences in a notebook she has already lost twice.
She has been here eleven days and is still testing which of her spells the local physics will tolerate.
She is looking for the version of this world where the door back is still standing open.
She says she is only passing through. She has said that in nine dimensions.
She has decided to treat this reality as a fresh sheet, and to stop counting.
She woke on Ritual Island with the tide out, alone, and started walking inland.
What she wants here is small and specific and she will not say what it is.
She is hunting whoever wrote her name into that ritual, across as many worlds as it takes.
For now she works for whoever pays, and asks the locals careful questions about their gods.

emRestlessLines: I'm the real protagonist here, you know.
I know a spell or two. Possibly more than I should.
This whole game plays better from my side of it.
Pick me and I promise hours of properly strange adventures.
I'm dimensionally immortal. Try and stop me.
Witches never dies! ...you know what I mean.
Ninety-two percent of my memories are gone and I'm still the best option on this board.
Still waiting. I've got all the time there is, technically.
emOriginalLore: Born in Wimbledon, Britannia, in 1984, on the branch where the Ritual actually happened: this is dimension three, the original. She gave up ninety-two percent of her memories to forge the spear that killed the Father aspect of YHWH, and woke on Ritual Island with no past and a magical potential that has been growing past what she can hold ever since. Every other Em fell here from somewhere else; she never had anywhere to fall from.
emBackstory: Em was born in {town}, Britannia, and wanted to be a witch in an age that had filed magic away with the fairy tales.

When Margaret Thatcher, quietly one of the three pillars of the Mage Guild, needed a fulcrum for the Solomonic Ritual, she picked Em. Em offered herself as the sacrifice. The price was ninety-two percent of her memories.

They did not go anywhere. They were forged into the Lance of Memory, the spear that killed the Father aspect of YHWH: his soul was scattered into quadrillions of fragments, his rotting body still orbits the Earth, and every sacred spell the Vatican knew stopped working that night.

She did not die on the table. She woke alone on Ritual Island on the first of January with no past at all and, for reasons nobody has been able to explain, a magical potential grown enormously past what she started with. She is still learning to hold it, and it is still growing.

She travels with Bubba and the camper they share, pointed at Beagle for an appointment she barely remembers. Bubba feels nothing for her and still loves Eris; Eris, goddess of discord and current occupant of the celestial throne, is jealous enough to bend cosmic law and probability to make Em's life hell.

tutorialClass.2: A pure spellcaster with the widest spread of elements in the game: fire, lightning, wind and ice from the very first fight, so there is an answer to whatever the enemy resists. Everything runs on mana, so learning to pace it is the whole craft. The convoking line is what no other caster gets: one great spell binds a familiar that then fights on its own until the battle ends.
tutorialClass.18: Fights on stamina instead of magic, and earns that stamina by brawling rather than starting with it, so the opening turns are thin and the later ones are not. The damage is raw strength, and almost every move is quick enough to land first. Half the list is aimed at the party rather than the enemy: the cheering is the real output, and it lasts the whole fight.
tutorialClass.16: Two trades in one, deliberately. The guns are quick and precise and exist to strip the enemy down: every shot takes away strength, toughness or both. The spells finish what the shooting opened. Whichever half has been spent, there is always something left to do, which is why the class never has a dead turn.
tutorialClass.64: Has no attacks of its own and borrows everybody else's. Mimic reads the enemies' whole repertoire for nothing and adds it to yours for the fight; Shapeshift goes further and swaps your body, health and skills for theirs. What the class can do is therefore entirely down to what it is facing: superb against a boss with a deep repertoire, nearly useless against something that only swings.
tutorialClass.22: A holy fighter who keeps the party on its feet while punishing the enemy with sacred light. Judgment falls on the whole field, Holy Water heals everyone and washes off five different afflictions at once, and Divine Sparks charges the party's magic. Sacred is the element the undead can least stand, so the damage reads modest on paper and lands hard.
tutorialClass.49: The only class here that fights for free. PSI Blast never costs anything and the rest costs almost nothing, so a psyker never runs dry and never needs a turn to recover. The power comes from the mind and goes straight past armour, and Trauma Cascade leaves an enemy confused without fail. Built to shut down enemy casters, weakest against things that do not think.
tutorialClass.35: A force multiplier. Nothing here is aimed at an enemy: every song lifts the whole party, the songs pile on top of one another, and they hold until the battle ends. A bard alone does nothing and raises everyone else's ceiling, so the worth grows with the length of the fight and with how good the rest of the party already is.
tutorialClass.12: A caster who steers the fight rather than ending it. Armor Curse strips the armour off every enemy at once, Familiar's Curse saps one enemy and leaves them taking far heavier blows, and Thesis Defense drains an enemy's magic instead of their health, stranding a caster with nothing to cast. Every turn is expensive, and every turn changes the shape of the fight.
tutorialClass.5: A summoner, and the slowest starter here. Convoke Spirits puts spirits on the field that fight on their own turns for free; everything else is what you do while the power builds back up. Shadow Pack is the cheapest way anyone on this board has of hurting a whole crowd. Very fragile until the field is full, very hard to stop once it is.
tutorialClass.3: Pure support. Holy Sacrament heals everybody, lifts three afflictions and wards off new ones; Divine Healing pulls a single ally back from the edge. Luminous Cascade is the only real damage, holy light over the whole field. A nun adds almost nothing to the damage and decides whether the damage matters.

tutorialSkill.1500: Binds a familiar that fights beside you until the battle ends, taking a turn of its own every round and asking nothing for it. It does no damage itself, so call it early: the longer the fight runs, the more free turns you get out of it.
tutorialSkill.415: A ball of fire thrown at one enemy, and the witch's hardest hitting attack. It usually leaves them Burned, which keeps taking health off round after round.
tutorialSkill.406: A jolt of lightning that lands before almost anything else on the field. The damage is small on purpose; what you want is Static, which leaves the target crackling and far more open to further lightning.
tutorialSkill.409: A gust that lifts one enemy off the ground and leaves them Floating. A floating target drifts out of reach of a great deal of ordinary fighting, though it is wide open to lightning.
tutorialSkill.1501: Opens the convoking rite, the door the larger summons come through. It does nothing by itself, so only spend a turn on it when you mean to spend the next ones on what it opens.
tutorialSkill.417: A shard of ice that strikes early and leaves the enemy Cold: chilled through, slower and easier to hurt. It makes them clumsier too, so aim it at whatever is hitting the party hardest.
tutorialSkill.1104: Plays to the crowd and lifts everybody: the whole party turns Inspired, which makes their spells cheaper, and their psychic power rises with it. Cheap and long lasting, so it is a fine first move in any fight that will not end quickly.
tutorialSkill.85: A net thrown and a strike that lands before the enemy can move. It usually leaves them Grappled: held in a lock, unable to dodge, and taking heavier blows from everything that follows.
tutorialSkill.61: A turn spent settling into stance, which leaves the wrestler stronger and tougher. It gives back more than it costs in a long fight and nothing at all in a short one.
tutorialSkill.67: The defensive half of the same trade: guard up, footwork tighter, quicker hands and more weight behind them. Take it when the party expects to be hit rather than to hit.
tutorialSkill.124: An uppercut that lands first and knocks the enemy off the ground with Floating. The damage is light; being in the air is the point, since it puts them out of reach for the turn.
tutorialSkill.1049: A patient shot that wears down the enemy's toughness and leaves them Unbalanced, so they swing wide and may lose their action altogether. The cheapest useful thing a gunmancer can do.
tutorialSkill.1037: A shot at close range that cuts both the enemy's strength and their toughness and often leaves them Bleeding, losing health every round. Fire it at whatever is hurting the party most.
tutorialSkill.1042: A round that goes straight through armour and leaves the target far less able to soak a hit. It does little on its own and makes everything the party does afterwards land harder.
tutorialSkill.848: A bolt of raw magic that dulls the enemy's wits. It is the gunmancer's fallback on any turn where the guns need a rest but the magic is still there.
tutorialSkill.1714: A dart of fire that strikes early, sets the enemy Burned so they keep losing health, and leaves them clumsier. It piles onto everything the guns have already stripped away, which is the whole point of carrying both.
tutorialSkill.3: Reads every enemy's entire repertoire and adds it to yours for the rest of the battle, and it costs nothing at all. It is simply the first move of any fight worth winning: whatever they know how to do, you now know how to do.
tutorialSkill.344: Sharpens the mimic's mind and grants Perfect Focus, so every blow lands as a critical while the guard stays thin. A cheap turn of preparation: everything borrowed afterwards is used at full power.
tutorialSkill.363: Takes the target's shape outright, their build, their health, their skills and their body, for the rest of the fight. The strongest thing the class does, so spend it on the biggest thing on the field and not on the first thing you see.
tutorialSkill.1933: Throws the last move an enemy used straight back at them. Cheap, and at its best right after something has spent its turn on a big attack.
tutorialSkill.859: Sparks fall over the whole party: their psychic power rises and Arcane Surge makes their magic far stronger, at the price of a slow drain on their mana. An opening move that pays for the rest of the fight.
tutorialSkill.574: Blessed water splashed over the party: a little healing for everyone, and Poison, Blind, Silence, Confusion and Nausea all washed off in one go. Cheap enough to use before the party is really in trouble.
tutorialSkill.1811: A mote of holy light that strikes early, blinds the enemy so half their swings go wide, and wears at their toughness. Sacred is what the undead can least stand, so it hurts them far more than the size of it suggests.
tutorialSkill.531: Trades away some of the paladin's own health for a much stronger will. A deliberate bargain, worth taking only when the damage coming in is magical and the health can be spared.
tutorialSkill.1731: Holy light on every enemy at once, resolved after almost everyone else has moved, often leaving them blinded and missing. The clearing move: it falls on a field the party has already softened.
tutorialSkill.957: A run of psychic hits that costs nothing at all, ever. It is what a psyker does on every turn not spent on something cleverer, and it is why the class never has to stop and recover.
tutorialSkill.959: Drains the life out of one enemy and puts it into the psyker. Almost free, and the reason a psyker can hold out through a long fight with nobody healing them.
tutorialSkill.962: Tears the enemy's mind open: they are left Confused and lashing out at random, usually asleep on top of it, and much duller for the rest. Point it at an enemy caster; it takes away what they cast with, then takes away their turn.
tutorialSkill.972: Reads the enemy and steadies the psyker: a sharper mind and Perfect Focus, which turns every blow into a critical while leaving the guard thin. Worth far more before the fight goes wrong than after.
tutorialSkill.966: Hurts an enemy and Provokes them, so they come at the psyker instead of anyone else. Use it to pull something dangerous off whoever cannot survive it.
tutorialSkill.1092: A simple tune that toughens the whole party and holds until the battle ends. The cheapest useful thing anybody in the party can do with a turn.
tutorialSkill.1106: A song that lends the party strength and leaves them Inspired, so their spells cost less. It piles onto the bard's other songs, so the order does not matter but playing them all does.
tutorialSkill.1256: A few minutes of limbering up, and the bard is quicker for it. Worth a turn only in a long fight, and only before the songs, so that everything after it is played better.
tutorialSkill.1170: Marches the party forward: everyone hits harder and gains Perfect Focus, landing critical after critical with their guard left open. The bard's strongest opener whenever the plan is to hit things until they stop.
tutorialSkill.850: An argument that drains the enemy's magic instead of their health. Against an enemy caster it wins the fight without touching them: no magic left, nothing to cast.
tutorialSkill.846: An enchantment laid over the whole party: more strength, and Arcane Surge to make their magic far stronger while it quietly drinks their mana. Expensive, so it earns its keep only in a fight long enough to spend it.
tutorialSkill.777: A curse that saps the enemy's strength and toughness and leaves them Vulnerable, taking much heavier blows. The cheap way to make something hit softer and break easier for the rest of the fight.
tutorialSkill.401: A puff of magic that leaves the enemy Unbalanced: clumsy, wide of the mark and liable to lose the turn entirely. The damage is incidental; keeping them from landing anything is the point.
tutorialSkill.810: Rots the armour off every enemy at once and leaves the whole field far easier to hurt. Expensive, and the single best turn an enchanter can spend against a crowd, because everything the party does afterwards lands harder.
tutorialSkill.1499: Calls spirits to the party's side, and from then on they fight on their own turns and ask nothing for it. The class's whole plan: cast it first, live through the turns it costs, and let the field do the work.
tutorialSkill.1295: A lesser convoking that saps one enemy's strength and toughness and leaves them Unbalanced, likely to stumble and lose their action. What a convoker does with the turns while the power for the real rite rebuilds.
tutorialSkill.1301: A scream that resolves after everyone else has moved, leaving the enemies Confused and mostly asleep. Cast it into a crowd the party has already engaged: it lands after their moves and clears up whatever survived.
tutorialSkill.1303: A pack of shadows set on every enemy, twice each, often leaving them Bleeding and losing health every round. By far the cheapest way this class has of hurting a whole crowd, and the answer whenever there is more than one enemy.
tutorialSkill.1930: Sends away whatever the party is holding on the field. Used to clear out a summon about to be turned against you, or to make room for a better one.
tutorialSkill.557: A sacrament over the whole party: healing for everyone, Poison, Blind and Silence lifted, and a ward that keeps new afflictions from taking hold at all. The opening move against anything that fights with curses rather than blows.
tutorialSkill.815: Slows every enemy on the field, so their blows come clumsily and go wide far more often. Expensive, and it makes the whole party harder to hit for the rest of the fight.
tutorialSkill.572: A vision granted to the whole party: more strength, more toughness, and Perfect Focus, so every blow is a critical while the guard stays open. The most expensive turn the class has, and usually the one that decides a hard fight.
tutorialSkill.566: A cascade of holy light over every enemy, often blinding them so their attacks go wide. The nun's only real damage, and worth far more against the undead than it looks.
tutorialSkill.536: Pours a great deal of health back into one ally. Far more per head than the prayer that covers everybody, so save it for someone nearly down rather than for a party that is merely scratched.
